methodological_rigor.justification: Integrated mechanistic study combining CRISPR screening, cell biology, transcriptomics, and in vivo xenograft experiments. Dual OSGEP-knockout/knockdown approaches to validate gene targets. Proper controls (parental vs. OSGEP-deficient cells, vehicle vs. treatment groups). Statistical testing with multiple independent replicates. In vivo tumor experiments with multiple mice per group. Limitations: single patient-derived transcriptomic data, limited validation of RIG-I activation mechanism in primary human melanoma samples.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical case-control study using melanoma cell lines and xenografts demonstrating therapeutic vulnerability through t6A tRNA modification. Identifies OSGEP as actionable target in melanoma; shows mechanistic link between translation dysfunction, stress granule formation, and RIG-I activation. OSGEP-driven signature correlates with T-cell infiltration and survival in patient cohort. Strong translational potential but requires prospective clinical validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for CRISPR screening, transcriptomics, immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, and in vivo tumor models. Animal protocols with ethics approval referenced. Transcriptomic data referenced (likely in GEO/ArrayExpress). Detailed mechanism of action descriptions. Some supplementary data referenced. Limited explicit statement on raw data availability or code sharing for CRISPR screening analysis.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel discovery that t6A tRNA modification deficiency disrupts melanoma proteostasis to enable anti-tumor immunity. OSGEP-RIG-I connection is new. Identifies previously unrecognized immune evasion mechanism through translation efficiency. Connects tRNA modification biology (emerging field) to cancer immunology. Demonstrates translational potential through patient signature correlation.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript progressing from functional genomics screening through mechanism identification to clinical correlation. Clear figures demonstrating OSGEP knockout effects, RIG-I relocalization, immune activation, and patient outcomes. Supplementary materials appropriately support main findings. Discussion contextualizes findings within immunotherapy resistance literature.

key_strengths: Unbiased functional genomics screen identifies OSGEP as driver of immune evasion in melanoma through tRNA modification control
Elegant mechanistic clarity: OSGEP loss → defective ANN codon translation → protein aggregation → RIG-I activation → anti-tumor T-cell response
OSGEP-driven gene signature associates with T-cell infiltration and improved overall survival in patient samples, supporting clinical relevance
Targets actionable node in protein synthesis pathway with potential broad applicability across immune-evasive cancers
key_concerns: Patient cohort analysis limited to signature correlation; lacks functional validation of OSGEP in human primary melanoma specimens
RIG-I mechanism partially explored; stress granule-mediated RIG-I activation requires deeper mechanistic characterization
Single-agent efficacy in xenografts; synergy with checkpoint inhibitors or other immunotherapies not explored in this study
Transferability to other cancer types remains unclear; clinical path to OSGEP inhibitor development not discussed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: solid preclinical work with robust mechanistic insights and clinical correlation data supporting further investigation of tRNA modification as immunotherapy target. Appropriate for Cancer Cell or similar high-impact journals; ready for clinical translation planning.
